target_customer: Full-time online creators (initially those with 100,000+ followers), later agencies, freelancers and small and mid-sized businesses that want banking, a charge card and payments
problem: Traditional banks and card issuers underwrite on credit scores and do not understand creator income, so creators with real revenue struggle to get credit and business banking.
business_model: Fintech (not a bank) earning card interchange and banking fees, with credit funded by equity plus debt facilities; underwrites on social metrics and platform revenue
product_category: Creator business banking and charge cards

founders.name: Eric Wei
founders.background_notes: Background from the YC company page and TechCrunch (2020-06-25).

founders.name: Will Kim
founders.background_notes: Described as an investor with seed fund Lucky Capital in TechCrunch (2020-06-25). Education not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to build card issuing and banking on top of partner banks and design a creator-specific underwriting model using follower and platform revenue data, which is standard fintech engineering plus a novel credit model.

defensibility.rationale: Karat relies on partner banks for charters and issuance, so there is no licence moat. Early differentiation was creator underwriting data and a creator-focused brand, which rivals could copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found that incumbents copied the creator card as of the sources read. The 2020 TechCrunch article only contrasts Karat with traditional banks.

market_need_then: In 2020 Wei said banks rarely understood creators' businesses or offered good terms, and he estimated a base of about 1 million full-time creators with 100,000+ followers (TechCrunch, 2020-06-25).

branding.domain_note: Company site uses trykarat.com, not karat.com; the site footer says it is not affiliated with Karat, Inc.

identity.visual_style: Product centered on a black card (the Karat Black Card)
identity.voice_and_tone: Growth and creator focused marketing copy

branding.community_and_virality: Launch cards were given to well known creators including TheRussianBadger, TierZoo and Nas Daily, and celebrity investors such as Jared Leto and Josh Richards were reported (fintech.global, 2021-07-02).

brand_strength.rationale: Creator and celebrity endorsements gave it visibility in the creator economy, but no source shows broad consumer brand recognition, and the name is shared with other Karat entities.

outcome_analysis: Karat launched out of YC W20 with a creator-specific black card and a $4.6M seed in June 2020, then raised a $26M Series A in 2021 and a $70M Series B in 2023 with a Visa partnership. The creator niche, a founder with Instagram product experience and celebrity creator distribution drove early traction, and debt facilities funded card balances. No shutdown or acquisition was found; much of the Series A and B headline totals are debt rather than equity.
notes: Series A of $26M was reported by other coverage as $11M equity plus $15M debt (Tubefilter via search snippet). Series B of $70M was $40M equity and $30M debt per TechCrunch. Clay lists a March 2020 seed with no amount, which conflicts with the June 2020 $4.6M report; the June figure is used. Aggregators list different founding years. The 2020 launch coverage names no rival products, only traditional banks; aggregator competitor lists (Novo, NorthOne, Bluevine, Found) are undated and not used. Karat's seed and Series A investors from the secondary snippet; USV lead from TechCrunch via search result text.
